summary.tagline: Discover the UK’s only dual UNESCO World Heritage Site, a remote archipelago of sea stacks and seabirds.

travel.headline: St Kilda Access and Sailing Reservations
travel.reservation: Access to this remote archipelago requires booking a spot with specialized boat operators departing from the Outer Hebrides. Because landings are highly weather-dependent, visitors must verify the current status and departure feasibility directly with their chosen charter service before travel.

days.title: Remote Heritage and Atlantic Wildlife
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Outer Hebrides

stops.name: St Kilda
stops.detail: Explore the abandoned village of Hirta and view the world's largest colony of Atlantic puffins among towering sea stacks.

days.driving: Allow several hours for the boat crossing; conditions vary significantly.
days.note: Expect significant maritime exposure; schedules are dictated by North Atlantic sea states.

intel.title: Maritime Reach
intel.text: The islands are reached via boat from the Outer Hebrides. Direct landings depend entirely on favorable swells at Village Bay.

intel.title: Seasonal Planning
intel.text: Trips are generally restricted to the summer months when sea conditions are most stable. Check with local operators for specific seasonal sailing windows.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Connectivity is not documented in available evidence for this remote archipelago. Visitors should assume a lack of cellular signal and prepare for an off-grid experience.

intel.title: Island Provisions
intel.text: There are no fueling stations or supply shops on the uninhabited islands. Ensure all personal requirements are met in the gateway towns of the Outer Hebrides before departure.

intel.title: Gateway Departure
intel.text: Parking is located at the various ferry and charter terminals on the mainland of the Outer Hebrides. Availability varies by specific departure point; consult your boat operator for local advice.

plan.arrival: Arrival involves a long boat journey from the Outer Hebrides; check in with your maritime charter at the designated pier for boarding instructions.
plan.vehicle: No vehicles are allowed on the archipelago; travel is strictly by boat and foot.
plan.goldenHour: Village Bay during the long summer twilight offers views of the dramatic sea stacks and stone cleits.
